summary: A heat pump can very likely heat this house, but whether the existing radiators are big enough is still open. The bill and the house size point to different heat loads, so the bill should be checked first. The single-pipe system must be checked by a technician.

thresholds.result: yellow: needs 55-60 C, higher running cost
needs > 60 C: some radiators should be upgraded

boundaries.how: Side photo of a typical radiator plus its height and width

reasons.text: Single-pipe system: radiators further along the loop get cooler water, so the last ones may need a higher flow temperature.
Radiator type unknown: the house runs with Type 33 at about 44-59 C, with Type 22 at about 50-71 C, with Type 11 at about 65-97 C.
The two heat-load estimates disagree (by area 12.8-19.2 kW, by bill 9.0-10.6 kW).

homeowner_can_provide: Side photo of one typical radiator, plus its height and width
Does the bill cover a full year and all heated rooms, and is any other heat source used?
Current flow temperature setting of the boiler, if known
technician_checks: Single-pipe loop: hydraulics and flow temperature at the last radiator
Outdoor unit placement, sound and permits
assumptions: Full-load hours 1800-2100 h (official approx. 2,000; range ours)
Radiator size unknown: assumed 600 x 1000 mm
Radiator output vs temperature: EN 442, n = 1.3, 10 K spread
Heat pump also covers hot water, at the same JAZ as space heating
